title: Port-Gentil taxi drivers stop work over municipal blouse requirement
scope: Reported citywide taxi service stoppage; the report does not establish a public gathering or link the action to other locations.
organizer: Unknown; FEGASTA appears in an earlier warning, but organizer of the July 31 stoppage is not explicit.

state_target.evidence: Municipal blouse/uniform requirement and related transport controls are described as the dispute; the local municipality is the apparent target.

demands_original: Opposition to a municipal uniform/blouse requirement and associated cost and controls.
participants_original: No count; report describes stopped taxis and unusually empty streets.
threshold_50_evidence: A strike-related citywide service disruption does not establish 50 people simultaneously gathered at a public action.

start_date.summary: Gabonclic dates the citywide taxi stoppage to July 31.

end_date.summary: Neither opened report gives a verified end date.

location.summary: Both reports concern Port-Gentil; the stoppage report says taxis stopped across the city.

scope.summary: The July 31 report describes a citywide taxi work stoppage. July 24 is only a union meeting/warning and is not merged as an event.

organizer.summary: The reports identify FEGASTA/transport unions in the warning context, but do not establish which organizers called the July 31 stoppage.

state_target.summary: Municipal blouse/uniform requirement and related transport controls are described as the dispute; the local municipality is the apparent target.

demands.summary: Drivers objected to the blouse requirement and associated cost/controls.

participants_original.summary: Article describes stopped taxis and empty streets, not people assembled.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: A strike-related citywide service disruption does not establish 50 people simultaneously gathered at a public action.

protester_violence.summary: No protester violence is reported in the opened accounts.

state_response.summary: No event-linked state response to the July 31 stoppage is documented; a July 30 municipal consultation lead is not evidence of response to this later event.

notes: The July 24 union meeting and July 30 city consultation are not counted as public protest or response to this July 31 event.
open_questions: Did 50 or more people gather simultaneously in a public action, rather than drivers only stopping work?
Was the July 31 stoppage organized by FEGASTA or another named group?
When did the stoppage end, and was it continuous with a later August action?
Was there an event-linked municipal response after the July 31 stoppage?
